#Coral_03 #Blasted Steps Skip 2
I’ve done a little bit of research regarding this skip and have some examples to show.
The main takeaway is that if you collide with the wall at all, you always have at least **1 frame** in which you can press jump. How many frames you actually have depends on how far you are up. 

There will be a few example videos, the first showing a scenario in which I slide off the wall, followed by an example of getting a walljump without cling. The main thing is that the first frame you collide with the walls, and the subsequent frames you are colliding with the wall, you are able to walljump, regardless of if hornet visually shows a cling grip state or not. The second video shows a successful BS2 in which I press jump the first possible frame without clinging. 

The third video shows 3 examples, the first being pressing jump without cling on the third frame of collision. The second is of pressing jump 2f early (in a scenario in which I wouldn’t get cling), and the third is a sample cling grip. It seems if roughly half of hornets hitbox collides with the wall then she will cling.

If you cling grip you have 7 frames before downward acceleration starts, combined with the time it takes to slip off this means a clingged jump usually have at least 10f (0.167s) or so to be inputted from the wall. Conversely, in my own experience most non-clingged attempts have roughly 3-4f which you’re able to jump off of.

A lot of attempts you won’t get high enough to cling, but you will be able to hit this **3-4f window and still get the skip.**
Practically speaking, most of the time trying to hit the window registers mentally as pressing comically early

Moss mother: doesn't save a hit
Bell beast: doesn't save a hit
Lace 1: no time to taunt
Moorwing: no time to taunt
Widow: Taunting before P1 and P2 does save 1 total hit, but other options are better
Last Judge: no time to taunt
Phantom: **Taunting saves 1 hit**
Dancers: ** Taunting saves 1 hit on Phases 1, 2, and 3** (not 4)
Trobbio: **Taunting saves 1 hit**
Lace 2: no time to taunt
GMS: doesn't save a hit

This does not account for taunting DURING a fight, which is viable on bosses like Last Judge and Trobbio. Also keep in mind that taunts are technically worse silk:damage ratio than Silkspears, but when done right they don't cost any time. I re-worked Scotty's version of this skip to avoid having to do the precise jump off the platform. I haven't played around with it a ton yet, but I think it has potential. Here's the steps I follow to do this:

- When jumping to the platform below the flying enemy, float underneath its aggro range to avoid waking it up.
- Dash into the wall and walljump, holding right until you're just past the background flag.
- Dash left and immediately hold right so that you begin a sprint turnaround the moment you land. You want to be fairly far right on the platform so you're close enough to cause the flying enemy to away, to the right.
- Sprint jump a moment after landing, aiming to jump over the flying enemy.
- If you clear the flying enemy, turn around and pogo it. You should pogo the top of its hitbox, not the side. If you jump into the enemy and get hit, you can still pogo it and make it to the right side. You can also make this step easier by hitting cloak just a moment before doing the pogo to help yourself line it up, but I'm not sure how consistent that is. 
- You can use the chain as a visual cue for timing your dash -> cloak repress in the air. I like to dash and repress cloak just before it.

#Greymoor_03 #Any% Craw Pogo 2 intricacies
So this is going to be a bit long, but bear with me. In the beggining you sprint on the ceiling up until the point of aggroing the second craw, but dont go too far to not make the first craw go to your right. After they are both on your left side, you should always be able to reach the higher platform with one pogo regardless of the craw that dives or at what time the dive happens. When im up there, i like to stand a little bit to the right of the ledge without jumping.

Now there are two scenarios that can happen, if the craw you hit is lower than the other one, its the good scenario (first clip), if not, its the bad scenario (second clip). For both skips i start with a jump and a pogo little after the higher craw passes the height of the ledge.

For the first clip, you should keep them both to your left for most of the climb, doing one pogo on the higher craw, then hit him again, followed by the other one, use a spear, then you should separate them to not get stuck under the platform.

For the second clip, you will do the pogo on the higher craw again, but this time youll pogo the lower one twice in a row, with a spear in the middle, this should separate them. Then youll just need to continue the climb using one more spear (always use them when youre closer to the craw on the left to make sure you dont go too far to the right). In the clip i did two more spears, but its bc i didnt notice i was already high enough.

Adding a few notes on the setup for this skip originally posted by QAQ https://discord.com/channels/772964112908156938/1423484610150666442/1423484834499657788
This is what I personally look out for during this skip:
- After the sprint jump off the ledge, I use flew brew at the very peak of my jump. The reason why using flea brew in the first place is important, is because it allows you to move faster in the air and get more distance after the damage boost towards the final ledge grab.
- At this time I look at the flower position. This is the most important part, because it helps me decide in what position I want to heal and how much I want to space out the inputs. If you heal too early/too far from the flower's range, you won’t trigger its attack/you will trigger it too late. If you heal too late/too far into the flower's range, you won't have enough time to dash out of the heal before taking damage. Its range is like a circle, so you want to heal on the outer edge of that circle - earlier if the flower is lower, later if it's higher.
This is an example of a small streak with different rng.
1st, 4th, 5th, 7th attempts = I can see that the flower is pretty low. This is usually the easiest rng (and what seems to be the most common) as there is a pretty big room for when to heal. In this case I want to dash and then heal pretty much immediately, since being horizontally closer to the flower makes you get hit by its attack sooner. In attempts 1, 4, and 7 I could've even healed much earlier after the dash and it would've still worked.
2nd attempt= The flower seemed kind of in the middle, not too high, not too low. I heal slightly later after the dash so that I get in its range.
3rd, 6th attempts = The flower looked pretty far up, which is the hardest rng. I try to space out my inputs as much as possible, but not too much that I start to lose height. Example 6 was probably the tightest here.

Some more strats for hokers of varying practicality.
1. You can pogo the hoker to bring him down and if you get very lucky it might get close enough to reach him with the taunt hitbox, which allows getting 5 (or maybe even 6, with one pogo) on a single hoker. This doesn't work well on the left hoker because it receives less knockback (idea from <@1021945170301829122>)
2. However it's still possible on the left one if you pogo it before it can shoot spines again, so it's never worth to do intentionally.
3. Using the back of the pogo hitbox allows you to reach higher and you don't need to be as close. There's also less risk of taking damage if you mess it up. It's generally useful for a lot of stuff here.
4. You can hit 3 spines with a single needle in this formation but it's precise
5. When running to the 2nd hoker you can jump preemptively
6. You don't need the explosion delay from the last hit to be able to get these 4 spines here. You can do this on the 2nd hit (or 1st i guess). Make sure that you pogo the hoker as low as you can to get as little height as possible. I find this easier with the backwards pogo.
7. You can also do it like this with a damage tank, but it's less consistent for me. You can experiment with it though, especially because knockback depends on the framerate, so it might be easier at the framerate you have.
8. You can do a similar thing for the plus pattern. Again, pogo as low as possible. For some reason this is easier for me with the normal pogo. This is pretty hard though for little reward at the cost of silk.
9. You can use the fireball to reach some spines at the ceiling. Hitting the rock with the spear from the left side usually brings the fireball straight down.
10. If you hit the rock with a needle instead, the fireball will usually end up next to the left wall. You can use it to get something from the ceiling if the hoker shot diagonally there. This is very impractical though (but funny).

#Dust_02 #Chalamet skip #cloakless
Saw many top runners doing this spear chalamet skip but couldn't find any setup/visual indicator guide so decided to make my own(sorry if this already exists).
- enter the transition while sprinting and keep sprinting until hornet clears this ring shaped background object after which you wanna jump (image 1).
- after jumping wait until hornet does the spin midair (she turns her head around like in image 2) at which point you want to input the dash and then pogo the enemy.
- after the pogo input immediately start holding right and when you reach the max height or clear this cage in the background (image 3) you want to spear towards the right.
- after the spear input let go of any direction and input a pogo while only holding down and no direction. you will pogo towards the right as you will be facing that way after the spear but still pogo the enemy.
- after this the enemy will move towards the left to attack and you can input a left downslash which will pogo you off the enemy and you can dash onto the cage.
This setup is very consistent. I have also attached a vid of me doing the skip 10 times in a row for reference.

#ant_02 #skarrgard #fleas #flea route #true ending #te #100 #hundo #all bosses #ab

Some strats for the Skarrgard at the entrance to Hunter's March (assuming you have Silkspear and nothing else)

The Skarrgard has 150 hp, so it's optimal to start the fight with at least 5/9 silk, though more than 5 doesn't hurt, and up to 7 can help. You can get 6 silk really easily/nearly optimally from the enemies on the way to the Skarrgard from Bell Beast (including 1 from the Silk Heart)

The Skarrgard has 3 possible moves - a swing, a jump, and a burrow. You can tell that the Skarrgard is going to swing when it draws back it's weapon, and you can pogo the Skarrgard between the two individual swings to get in an attack. The timing is fairly tight but very consistent after some practice (see attachment 1). For the jump and burrow, the visual indicator is the same - a slight crouch. However, there is an _audio_ indicator - if the Skarrgard growls before the attack, it will always be a jump. You should stay still if it is burrowing, and start moving towards the Skarrgard as soon as you _see_ that it is jumping, to avoid getting hit. It's very easy to get hit if you don't react quite quickly. It's nice to get into the habit of upslashing just before either of those attacks, both because niche timings can make it so that a regular slash will only hit the Skarrgard if it burrows and not if it jumps, and because the knockback from a regular slash makes it easier to get hit on a jump. Very rarely, the timings make it so that you have to do a minihop before the upslash to hit the Skarrgard on either attack. Attachments 2 and 3 are examples of what a jump and burrow should each look like.

(2 messages because of character limit)
You can almost always get in a Silkspear in between moves without getting hit, but you want land or do a turnaround to cancel the slash animation to both speed up the Silkspear and ensure that you don't get hit. Be careful about Silkspears after swings, as the Skarrgard can attack slightly earlier than usual if the previous and next attacks are both swings.

Ideally, you want to get in as many Silkspears when the Skarrgard is close the the right wall, so you can cancel the animation and get in extra nail hits. While the Skarrgard can end up there halfway through the fight, it is always there at the start. Attachment 4 is an example of an opening that lets you get in 2 Silkspears without getting hit that works for every move the Skarrgard could start with, assuming you start with 6 silk. You need to do _nearly_ a full jump when you get to the edge of the corpse, and pogo when you touch the far lantern... sort of. It's very vibe-based, and can be consitant with practice. You do that pogo, Silk Spear, nail slash, then turnaround animation cancel into another Silk Spear.

Finally, attachment 5 is an example of what an entire fight should look like.

Here's some stuff past me didn't figure out:

- The opening I had in the previous post was a bit scuffed and awkward. Attachment 1 is a slightly faster and more consistent version of it. As long as your jump is after the second twig and last pogo is after the rightmost edge of the rightmost bush, it should hit the Skarrgard. Due to random inconsistency during pogo dashes, you may be much higher or lower than I was in attachment 1, but nearly anything works. All of the attachments use this opening, so this variation can be seen between them.

- You can actually hit the Skarrgard an extra time during it's swing. This lets you kill it super fast if you get the perfect rng of 3 swings in a row (attachment 2).

- The only reason for an upslash before a jump or burrow is to avoid the knockback of a regular slash - don't bother upslashing on burrows. If you find it hard to avoid getting hit by walking under jumps, you can just not slash before a jump and focus on the movement, or you can do a slightly tricky parry (attachment 3). It's really hard (but possible!) to actually hit the Skarrgard with the parry, so try to focus on perfecting the timing before that.

Other than all that's it's straightforward. If you're just trying to survive, try to work on perfecting your responses to attacks and then recognising them in the context of the fight. If you're trying to go as fast as possible, you can work on adding the harder strats

# Cocoon Skip Skip Guide

Shoutouts to @Fallen and <@445108343002890246> for discovery/setup help

There's a few different setups for this trick,** however this is the best universal one from testing**. 

Skip seems to be unaffected by fps, tested between 50-600fps. Maintaining height is especially difficult below 60fps.

To get into the horizontal spot, neutral dash into the upper slope corner, as long as you clip the flat part we will jump off later your x position will stay 100% consistent. Use nail knockback when landing to end with a position of 21.90044, 249.56770. You can make a couple other spots work if you end up dashing too high/low on the slope, but this is the sweet spot.

Next you're going to neutral jump, and press flea brew when you have a Y velocity between 10.2 and 13.8. The best window is aiming 12.6. You can use debug input display or try to find the frame when hornets animation changes. Once you've pressed flea brew you can let go of jump at any point before it ends, and then buffer left+jump.

This should give you a wall jump, and you can turn back to the right afterwards and buffer floats out of clawline.

*Note this skip is not officially confirmed legal, but likely will be soon*

**Cloakless Memorium Walljump**
this is difficult. 

The way this walljump works is that you use flea brew to gain more height than a normal jump to be able to reach a jumpable wall.
This used to only be possible with cloak because of how it let you jump further and lower from a wall.

-# all testing done on 60fps

while brew is still in effect I hold right and don't hold jump
jump needs to be pressed on the frame (or frames after) hero state becomes airborne and are in the vertical range mentioned previously
after pressing jump, keep holding jump and right as that will land on the ledge above
the jump input will not work if the hero state is no_input (spamming might help, but it didn't work for me)
if you correctly timed a jump after airborne appears the jump can still fail if you are too low (missing the wall) or too high (bonking on the ceiling)

This skip is useful when going to the trap far fields flea after lace 1.

I think that the skip overall is simple, but the setup is somewhat rng.
All you need to do is pogo a Skarr Scout mid jump then pogo off of a breakable rock.

If it Jumps then you can pogo the skar and then pogo the rock, if it Throws you can attack to deflect the sickle, and if it Burrows try and keep the same distance that you started with while having the breakable rock between you and the skar.

There is good news because, if done correctly, it will always jump by the 3rd attack. So there aren't that many possibilities. 
I can't fit them all in this clip so all the possible variations from testing are listed here based on the attack used:
